prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the continuous layout of the indoor bouldering gym, showing a padded floor mat sloping away from the camera wearer (from ~0.5 m at the bottom edge to ~5–6 m at the base of the back wall) and an angled left wall ~2–4 m away. It tracks the person in the grey top standing on the mat ~3.5–4 m ahead and slightly left in frames 1–2, turning clockwise in frame 3, and walking slightly closer (~2.5–3 m) toward the centre-left in frames 4–5, while their head becomes cropped out by the top frame boundary. In frames 4–5, a bright white region at the bottom-left (~0.3–0.5 m) reveals the camera wearer's own left hand and knee, and in frame 5 a stark white silhouette extending from the bottom-right (~0.2–0.6 m) shows the wearer's outstretched right arm within arm's reach, partially occluding the distant person's right leg. Compared to the visually busy RGB wall holds and mat creases, the depth map makes the smooth 3D geometry of the floor-to-wall corner and the huge depth gap between the wearer's extended arm and the distant walker immediately obvious. However, the map is unreliable for the second person climbing high on the right wall (~4–5 m away and ~3–4 m to the right of the standing person), who is only faintly visible in frame 1 and completely merges into the dark background wall in frames 2–5, and it also flattens the protruding geometric climbing volumes on the walls.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the standing person on the left mat across all five frames with sharp pink masks, showing their shift from facing away (~3.5–4 m ahead) in frames 1–2, to right profile in frame 3, to facing toward the camera wearer (~2.5–3 m away) in frames 4–5 with their head cropped at the top edge. In frame 1, it also detects the second climber ~4–5 m away on the upper-right wall (whose holds are within that climber's arm's reach), and in frame 5 it segments the camera wearer's extended right arm in the foreground (~0.2–0.6 m) as a separate 'person' mask overlapping the distant walker's lower legs. Unlike the RGB image where dark clothes blend into the dark blue mat and multi-coloured holds, the segmentation map provides crisp object boundaries for the detected figures and clearly delineates the occlusion boundary where the wearer's fist overlaps the distant person's shin in frame 5. However, the map is highly unreliable in several ways: it misses the right-wall climber entirely in frames 2–4 (where they become partially cropped at the right edge), misses the wearer's bottom-left body part in frames 2–5, misclassifies the standing person's brightly coloured climbing shoes and mat creases as 'skateboard' in frames 1 and 3, and hallucinates a large 'umbrella' mask over the upper-left climbing wall in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders yellow 2D body skeletons on a black background, capturing the standing person on the left mat in frames 1, 2, and 3, while all other frames and regions remain completely blank. In frames 1 and 2, the full-body skeleton (minus the cropped head in frame 2) shows the person ~3.5–4 m away to the upper-left with shoulders and hips aligned parallel to the back wall as they face away from the camera wearer. In frame 3, the skeleton compresses horizontally into a side-profile configuration with the right arm extending slightly forward, capturing the person's clockwise turn toward the right before they walk closer in later frames. This skeletal wire-frame makes the exact joint articulations of the knees, hips, and elbows and the transition from a rear stance to a side profile much easier to read than in the dark, baggy clothing of the RGB frames. However, the pose map is severely unreliable overall: it completely fails to detect the approaching person in frames 4 and 5 once their upper body is cropped at the top edge, fails to detect the second climber on the right wall across all five frames, and provides no hand keypoints (magenta) or skeletons for the camera wearer's own visible limbs within arm's reach.
